defectsFound.summary: Reading a configuration resource and writing the identical value back rewrites every `key =>` line as `key = >`, which Asterisk parses differently.
defectsFound.proof: An unchanged read -> stage round trip of /etc/asterisk/extensions.conf took the file from 61 `exten =>` lines to 0, and all 161 dialplan and include lines differed.
defectsFound.blastRadius: 13 of the shipped sample configuration files use the arrow form, 419 lines in total; several are configurable resources.
defectsFound.whyItSurvivedValidation: validate and post-read both compare the parsed structure, and the structure round-trips consistently, so neither can observe the textual corruption.

defectsFound.summary: ConfigTransaction takes a backup and completes the `backup:` action, but ApplyResult does not return the handle, so a caller cannot roll back a successful apply through the returned result.
defectsFound.proof: ApplyResult keys were planId, status, startedAt, finishedAt, completedActions, rollbackAttempted, message. Rollback was only reachable by taking a second backup in the caller before applying.
defectsFound.consequence: automatic rollback still works on a failed apply; a deliberate undo after a successful one has no supported route.
